activity.notes: Songtsen Gampo (Srong-brtsan sgam-po) is the early Tibetan imperial ruler under whom the Tibetan kingdom expanded and consolidated. UNESCO's History of Civilizations of Central Asia places his enthronement and rule at about 620 to 649/650. ATLAS therefore uses c.620–650 with approximate boundaries rather than choosing one of the competing 618/629 accession traditions as exact.

sources.title: History of Civilizations of Central Asia, Vol. III — The Western Regions under the T'ang Empire and the Kingdom of Tibet
sources.citation_text: UNESCO's scholarly history places the enthronement of Srong-brtsan sgam-po at about 620 and his death at 649 or 650, identifying him as btsan-po and describing his imperial institutions and expansion.

sources.title: Royal titulature and the succession to the throne in the Tibetan Empire — Bulletin of the School of Oriental and African Studies
sources.citation_text: A modern study of Tibetan imperial titulature and succession treats Khri Srong-rcan (Songtsen Gampo) as an attested ruler in the early imperial dynasty and discusses the documentary basis for the succession chronology.

review_context.correction_note: Register the historical Tibetan ruler under the Tibetan Empire rather than the generic game label 'Tibetan Civilization'.
